semantic_checks: Four actual complex-valued coefficient functions are real analytic on one positive-radius ball centered at the norm singularity, in a nontrivial real normed vector space.

Subtracting their two actual representations gives (a-c)+||x||(b-d)=0. The reviewed zero-decomposition theorem applies to the analytic differences, yielding a=c and b=d on the entire ball, including zero.

The parameter theorem applies this exact uniqueness statement independently at each parameter in the supplied arbitrary set. It does not assume parameter topology or analyticity and does not claim either.
The assumptions are equality of represented functions and analytic regularity of the coefficient functions. They do not assume coefficient-pair equality or a disguised equivalent premise.
limits: The result supplies uniqueness, not existence, of analytic coefficient pairs. The ball must include the norm singularity; no uniqueness on arbitrary balls away from zero is asserted.
